#!/bin/bash
# Compile-path ladder, restricted to the files this rung can affect.
#
# A copy of ../run-ladder.sh with two changes: the ladder root and output
# directory are private to this worktree, and the two whole-corpus loops are
# replaced by one driven by subset.txt (corpus<TAB>file per line).
#
# Pushes every interpreter test program (ProjectFortress/tests/*.fss) and every
# file in ProjectFortress/not_working_library_tests/ through the compiler path
# unchanged and records how far each one gets.
#
# Reproduce:  bash explorations/compile-ladder/run-ladder.sh
# Outputs:    explorations/compile-ladder/raw/<corpus>/<name>.{compile,run}
#             explorations/compile-ladder/results.tsv
#
# The run uses a private cache tree so it never touches default_repository/caches
# (fortress.caches system property + FORTRESS_CACHES env; ProjectProperties.java:283,
# same mechanism the suite uses at build.xml:941-943), and a private java.io.tmpdir
# so the 5.8 MB Rats! temp directory of every grammar-importing run (RatsUtil.java:138-144)
# is swept per file instead of filling the disk.

set -u

source "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../../../experiment/env.sh"

LADDER_ROOT="${LADDER_ROOT:-$FORTRESS_HOME/tmp/ladder-r1}"
export LADDER_CACHES="$LADDER_ROOT/ladder-caches"
export LADDER_TMP="$LADDER_ROOT/ladder-tmp"
export FORTRESS_CACHES="$LADDER_CACHES"
export JAVA_FLAGS="-Xmx2g -Xss64m -Dfortress.caches=$LADDER_CACHES -Djava.io.tmpdir=$LADDER_TMP"

PRISTINE="$LADDER_ROOT/pristine"
OUT="$FORTRESS_HOME/explorations/compile-ladder/repair-r1-atomic-static"
RAW="$OUT/raw"
TSV="$OUT/results.tsv"

COMPILE_TIMEOUT=120
RUN_TIMEOUT=60
MIN_FREE_KB=512000

mkdir -p "$RAW/tests" "$RAW/not_working_library_tests" "$LADDER_TMP"

disk_guard () {
    local free
    free=$(df -P / | awk 'NR==2{print $4}')
    if [ "$free" -lt "$MIN_FREE_KB" ]; then
        echo "STOP: only ${free} KB free on / (floor ${MIN_FREE_KB} KB)" | tee -a "$OUT/ladder.log"
        exit 2
    fi
    echo "-- disk free ${free} KB, cache $(du -sm "$LADDER_CACHES" | cut -f1) MB"
}

# Step 1: the compiler-world library, in the order repo-internals.md gives.
build_library () {
    cd "$FORTRESS_HOME/ProjectFortress" || exit 1
    local f
    for f in LibraryBuiltin/AnyType.fss LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss \
             ../Library/CompilerLibrary.fss ../Library/CompilerAlgebra.fss \
             ../Library/CompilerSystem.fss ; do
        echo "library: $f"
        timeout 600 ../bin/fortress compile "$f" || { echo "LIBRARY BUILD FAILED on $f"; exit 1; }
    done
}

# Step 2: one known-good compiled program must print PASS before the ladder starts.
sanity () {
    cd "$FORTRESS_HOME/ProjectFortress" || exit 1
    timeout 200 ../bin/fortress compile library_tests/Integer1.fss > /dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
    timeout 60 ../bin/fortress run Integer1 2>&1 | grep -q PASS
}

# Keep only the library's own cache entries; a program's entries are never reused.
prune_cache () {
    ( cd "$LADDER_CACHES" && find . -type f -print ) | sort > "$LADDER_TMP/.now"
    ( cd "$PRISTINE" && find . -type f -print ) | sort > "$LADDER_TMP/.keep"
    comm -23 "$LADDER_TMP/.now" "$LADDER_TMP/.keep" | while read -r p; do
        rm -f "$LADDER_CACHES/$p"
    done
}

component_of () {
    # component/api name as declared, which is what `fortress run` wants
    sed -n 's/^[[:space:]]*\(component\|api\)[[:space:]]\+\([A-Za-z0-9_.]\+\).*/\2/p' "$1" | head -1
}

run_one () {
    local corpus="$1" path="$2"
    local base name comp crc rrc t0 t1 ct rt
    base=$(basename "$path")
    name="${base%.*}"
    comp=$(component_of "$path")
    [ -n "$comp" ] || comp="$name"

    t0=$(date +%s)
    timeout -k 5 "$COMPILE_TIMEOUT" ../bin/fortress compile "$path" \
        > "$RAW/$corpus/$base.compile" 2>&1
    crc=$?
    t1=$(date +%s); ct=$((t1-t0))

    rrc=""
    rt=""
    if [ "$crc" -eq 0 ] && [ "${base##*.}" = "fss" ]; then
        t0=$(date +%s)
        timeout -k 5 "$RUN_TIMEOUT" ../bin/fortress run "$comp" \
            > "$RAW/$corpus/$base.run" 2>&1
        rrc=$?
        t1=$(date +%s); rt=$((t1-t0))
    fi

    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' \
        "$corpus" "$base" "$comp" "$crc" "$rrc" "$ct" "$rt" >> "$TSV"
    echo "$corpus/$base crc=$crc rrc=$rrc ${ct}s"
}

main () {
    echo "=== ladder start $(date -Is) ==="
    disk_guard
    if [ ! -d "$PRISTINE" ]; then
        build_library
        rm -rf "$PRISTINE"; cp -a "$LADDER_CACHES" "$PRISTINE"
    fi
    sanity || { echo "SANITY FAILED: library_tests/Integer1 did not print PASS"; exit 1; }
    echo "sanity ok: library_tests/Integer1 compiles and prints PASS"
    prune_cache

    : > "$TSV"
    cd "$FORTRESS_HOME/ProjectFortress" || exit 1

    local n=0 line corpus f
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r corpus f; do
        [ -n "$corpus" ] || continue
        run_one "$corpus" "$corpus/$f"
        n=$((n+1))
        rm -rf "${LADDER_TMP:?}"/fortress*rats
        if [ $((n % 10)) -eq 0 ]; then prune_cache; disk_guard; fi
    done < "$OUT/subset.txt"
    prune_cache
    echo "=== ladder done $(date -Is), $n files ==="
    disk_guard
}

main "$@"

    Exception => false
  end

run(): () = do

  println("IntegerOverflow caught from narrow of 2^32: " shouldOverflow(fn () => narrow(l)))
end

end

73: One way to think about coercion is that if type \VAR{T} can be coerced
74: to type \VAR{U}, then a value of type \VAR{T} can be used to ``stand
75: in'' for a value of type \VAR{U} in a functional call, for example.  This is
76: different from actually \emph{being} of type \VAR{U}; it means only
77: that, given any value of type \VAR{T}, an appropriate value of type
78: \VAR{U} can be computed to substitute for it.  Also, coercion occurs
79: only when the declared type of the corresponding parameter in the
80: functional declaration is exactly the type \VAR{U} being coerced to
81:  not if it is a supertype of \VAR{U}.  Note, however, that if type
82:  \VAR{T} can be coerced to type \VAR{U} then any subtype of \VAR{T}
83:  can also be coerced to type \VAR{U}.
84: 
85: Coercion from \VAR{T} to \VAR{U} may occur in an expression context
86: where the context expects the expression to have type \VAR{U} and
87: the type of the expression is a subtype of \VAR{T} except for the following
88: cases:
89: \begin{itemize}

91: \item type assumptions (see \secref{type-assumption})

# Rung W: widen, narrow, unsigned, signed

problem: `fib13[\NN32\](unsigned(20))` stops at disambiguate on `unsigned` and on nothing else — `ProjectFortress/tests/fib13.fss:30`

spec: none — no prose chapter names any of the four, and the rule the out-of-range decision rests on is "For integer results, overflow throws an `IntegerOverflow`" at `Specification/basic/operators/opr-overview.tex:155`

precedent: this world's own plainly-named signed narrowing, `getter asZZ32(): ZZ32 = jLongOverflowingToInt(self)`, whose body `narrow` reproduces verbatim — `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss:575`

deviation: `NN64.signed` is declared `: ZZ64` where the interpreter's api declares `: NN64`, because the glue it binds returns an `FLong` — `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/glue/prim/UnsignedLong.java:59-60`

deviation: `NN64.narrow` throws `IntegerOverflow` out of range where the interpreter truncates, so `ProjectFortress/tests/UnsignedTest.fss:210-211` will not hold on the compiled path — provisional ledger row W-2 below

deviation: the rung adds one native binding, `simpleUnsignedIntArith.toLong`, and not only declarations, because no imported native zero-extends an `NN32` into a long — `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss:85`

deviation: the rung also changes one body it did not add, `NN64.coerce(x: NN32)`, which sign-extended — `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss:809`

historical: `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fsi`, `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss`

## What landed

Eight declarations in `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fsi` and eight bodies in `.fss`, two in each of `trait ZZ32`, `trait ZZ64`, `trait NN32` and `trait NN64`, each declaration at the end of its trait body where the interpreter's own api puts them (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:493-495`, `:532`, `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fsi:105-107`).

| trait | declaration | body |
|---|---|---|
| `ZZ32` | `widen(self): ZZ64` | `jIntToLong(self)` |
| `ZZ32` | `unsigned(self): NN32` | `jMakeNN32FromZZ32(self)` |
| `ZZ64` | `narrow(self): ZZ32` | `jLongOverflowingToInt(self)` |
| `ZZ64` | `unsigned(self): NN64` | `jMakeNN64FromZZ64(self)` |
| `NN32` | `widen(self): NN64` | `jMakeNN64FromZZ64(jUnsignedIntToLong(jMakeZZ32FromNN32(self)))` |
| `NN32` | `signed(self): ZZ32` | `jMakeZZ32FromNN32(self)` |
| `NN64` | `narrow(self): NN32` | `jMakeNN32FromZZ32(jLongOverflowingToUnsignedInt(jMakeZZ64FromNN64(self)))` |
| `NN64` | `signed(self): ZZ64` | `jMakeZZ64FromNN64(self)` |

Two further changes, both in files the rung already owns. One new native binding, `simpleUnsignedIntArith.toLong => jUnsignedIntToLong` (`CompilerBuiltin.fss:85`), because the import block had no int-to-long conversion that zero-extends and `NN32.widen` needs one. And one repair: `NN64.coerce(x: NN32)` (`CompilerBuiltin.fss:809`) was `jMakeNN64FromZZ64(jIntToLong(jMakeZZ32FromNN32(x)))`, and `simpleLongArith.intToLong` is `(long) i` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nativeHelpers/simpleLongArith.java:302-304`), so it sign-extended: an `NN32` of 4294967295 coerced to `NN64` became 18446744073709551615.

Nothing else: no `.java`, no `.scala`, no `ant compileAll`, no prelude declaration changed, no declaration renamed or removed.

## Where this fix belongs

`explorations/coordinator/map/spec-to-implementation.md:323` puts the numeric tower's library side in the prelude column and §4.3 at `:399-410` says what the compiler prelude has of it: nothing above `Number`, and each fixed-size trait carries its own flat declarations. §4.1 at `:356` says the same of operators declared inside a trait — "the compiler prelude declares its own". So a conversion between two fixed-size integer traits is a prelude declaration and a prelude body, not a checker or a codegen change; `explorations/coordinator/map/modules-and-phases.md:449` and `:483-484` give the native mechanism it stands on, `import java` plus `nativeHelpers/`, which is what the bodies use.

The four names are functional methods, not getters: `widen(self): ZZ64` is invoked as `widen(x)`, which is the form `ProjectFortress/tests/fib13.fss:30`, `longPrim.fss:23`, `UnsignedTest.fss:17` and `NumberPrintTest.fss:52` all write, and the form the interpreter's api uses for the same four names.

## Precedent search

The question asked was "has the team solved this here already, and in how many ways", and the answer is in the file being edited.

**Widening `ZZ32` to `ZZ64`: one way.** `coerce(x: ZZ32) = jIntToLong(x)` (`CompilerBuiltin.fss:574`). `widen` uses the same native.

**Narrowing `ZZ64` to `ZZ32`: seven natives bound, one used.** The import block binds `longToInt` (`:33`), `longOverflowingToInt` (`:40`), `longLowHalfToInt` (`:41`), `longHighHalfToInt` (`:42`), `longMaskedToInt` (`:43`), `longWrappingToInt` (`:51`) and `longSaturatingToInt` (`:58`). Past the import block, `longOverflowingToInt` is used once — `getter asZZ32(): ZZ32` at `:575` — and `longLowHalfToInt` sixteen times, every one of them a shift count where truncation modulo the word width is the operation. The other five are used nowhere. So the plainly-named signed narrowing in this world already exists and it throws.

**Bit reinterpretation: four getters.** `ZZ64.bitsAsNN64` (`:577`), `ZZ32.bitsAsNN32` (`:660`), `NN32.bitsAsZZ32` (`:748`), `NN64.bitsAsZZ64` (`:812`). `unsigned` and `signed` are the functional-method spellings of exactly these four, and their bodies are the same four native calls.

**Widening `NN32` to `NN64`: one site, and it is wrong.** `jIntToLong(jMakeZZ32FromNN32(...))` appears once in the whole file, at `:809`, and `jIntToLong` appears twice in total (`:574`, `:809`). That is the count rule 2 asks for: one site, repaired here, and no second one.

**Narrowing `NN64` to `NN32`: three natives bound, none used.** `longOverflowingToUnsignedInt` (`:85`), `longWrappingToUnsignedInt` (`:93`) and `longSaturatingToUnsignedInt` (`:100`) are all imported and none is called anywhere in the file. The slot was reserved and never filled.

**The convention that decides which of the three to use.** In `trait NN32` and `trait NN64` the plainly-spelled member always takes the Overflowing native and the wrapping and saturating spellings take the other two: `opr +` takes `unsignedIntOverflowingAdd` at `:758` while `opr BOXPLUS` takes the Wrapping one at `:759` and `opr DOTPLUS` the Saturating one at `:760`, and the same triple runs through `-`, `DOT`, `CROSS`, `DIV`, unary `-`, `|self|`, `CHOOSE` and juxtaposition. Thirteen plainly-named members of those two traits take an Overflowing native; nineteen more do in `trait ZZ32` and `trait ZZ64`. `narrow` is a plain name, so by the file's own convention it takes `longOverflowingToUnsignedInt`.

**The interpreter, read in the glue rather than in the api.** `Int$ToLong` is `(long) x` (`interpreter/glue/prim/Int.java:221-224`), sign-extension, and `NN32$ToUnsignedLong` is `Unsigned.toLong(x)` (`NN32.java:237-241`), zero-extension — so `widen` is sign-extending on the signed side and zero-extending on the unsigned side, which is what the two bodies do. `ZZ32$ToNN32` (`ZZ32.java:213-217`), `NN32$ToInt` (`NN32.java:231-235`), `Long$ToUnsignedLong` (`Long.java:231-235`) and `UnsignedLong$ToLong` (`UnsignedLong.java:224-228`) all return their argument unchanged — `unsigned` and `signed` reinterpret bits. `Long$FromLong` is `Int.rc(x)` (`Long.java:237-241`), and `Int.rc` raises `error("Overflow of ZZ32 " + i)` when the value does not fit (`Int.java:239-245`). `UnsignedLong$FromLong` is `(int) x` (`UnsignedLong.java:230-234`), a silent truncation.

**No competing declaration.** No `.fss` under `ProjectFortress/tests/` or any `*_tests/` directory declares any of the four; the only other declarations in the tree are the interpreter prelude's own and `ProjectFortress/not_working_static_tests/BuiltinTest.fss:68,72`, which declares its own `widen` and `unsigned` inside its own trait and is not in a gated corpus. A whole-tree grep of `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/` for the four names as Fortress identifiers finds nothing: every hit for `widen` is the `widens` reserved word (`parser/Keyword.rats`, `nodes/WhereCoerces.java`, `scala_src/typechecker/impls/Operators.scala`) and every hit for `narrow` is `narrowToRange` or unrelated.

## The specification, and the decision it does not make

The four names are absent from the prose chapters. The grep, re-run 2026-09-20 over `Specification/basic/` and `Specification/basic-lib/`, finds five lines and not one of them is a declaration or a description of these functions: `basic/types-vals-vars.tex:508` and `:514` use "unsigned" as an adjective while listing the fixed-size type names, `basic-lib/objects.tex:63` and `:103` describe a hash code as an unsigned integer, and `basic-lib/basic-integers.tex:802` says "**k** bits suffice to represent this integer in unsigned binary form" about `integerLength`. `widen` appears only as the reserved word `widens` (`basic/conversions-coercions.tex:766`, `:784`), which is the automatic-widening mechanism of `\secref{widening}` — widest-need evaluation of an expression, described at `:771-787` in terms of promoting 32-bit floating-point operands before a product is computed — and is a different thing from a named conversion function. `basic-lib/basic-integers.tex` has one section, `\section{Integers}` at `:13`, and it specifies the methods of `ZZ`; there is no section for `ZZ32`, `ZZ64`, `NN32` or `NN64` anywhere under `basic-lib/`.

What the specification does say about a result that does not fit, read in full rather than grepped: `basic/operators/opr-overview.tex:154-159` and again verbatim at `:195-200`, "The handling of overflow depends on the type of the number produced. For integer results, overflow throws an `IntegerOverflow`." And `:205-209`, "Wraparound addition and subtraction on fixed-size integers are expressed by ∔ and ∸. Saturating addition and subtraction on fixed-size integers are expressed by ⊞ and ⊟. These operations do not overflow." — so the wrapping and the saturating behaviours have their own spellings and the plainly spelled one is the one that may overflow. `basic-lib/basic-integers.tex:368-370` is the same statement from the other side: on `ZZ` the wrapping and saturating operators "do exactly the same thing, because operations on type `ZZ` never need to wrap or saturate".

**The decision, and it is a decision: `narrow` throws `IntegerOverflow` when the value does not fit, on both the signed and the unsigned side.** Four things argue for it. The file's own convention, counted above: thirty-two plainly-named members of the four numeric traits take an Overflowing native, and the wrapping and saturating spellings take the other two. This world's own signed narrowing, `asZZ32` at `:575`, already throws, so a truncating `narrow` would put two plainly-named signed narrowings with different answers in one trait. The team's own import block reserved all three unsigned narrowings and used none, so the plain slot was left open and the convention says which of the three fills it. And the specification's twice-stated rule that an integer result that does not fit throws `IntegerOverflow`, with truncation given its own spelling elsewhere.

**What the alternative costs, since the alternative has real evidence behind it.** Truncating on the unsigned side is what the interpreter does (`UnsignedLong.java:230-234`) and what `ProjectFortress/tests/UnsignedTest.fss:210-211` assert, at the deliberately chosen out-of-range values 2^63 and 2^64-1: `widen(narrow(-x1)) = (x1 LSHIFT 32)-1` and `widen(narrow(x1 LSHIFT 63)) = x0`. Those two lines are gated: `ProjectFortress/tests/` holds 383 `.fss` and no `.test` file at all, and `FileTests.interpreterSuite("tests", true, false)` (`FileTests.java:768`) runs every one of them directly, so an `assert` that fails there turns `ant testSystem` red. The file passes today — measured, `probes/walk-unsignedtest.txt`, `PASS?` and exit 0. So choosing to throw makes those two assertions a walk-against-compiled divergence on the day `UnsignedTest.fss` compiles, and the specification does not settle it because it does not mention `narrow`. That divergence is measured both ways here and carried as provisional ledger row W-2; it is the price of the decision and it is not hidden. The two remaining arguments for truncating are weaker than they look: the interpreter's signed narrow raises an uncatchable Java-level error rather than a Fortress exception (measured, `probes/walk-narrow.txt`), so the glue is not a careful witness on this point; and the asymmetry it would install has no statement anywhere in the tree to support it.

## The failing test, and the pass

`ProjectFortress/library_tests/IntConversionsRungW.fss` and `IntConversionsRungW.test`, the latter in the form of `library_tests/IntegralOpsRungN.test`: `tests=IntConversionsRungW`, `link`, `run`, `run_out_contains=PASS`. `run_out_contains` is the key at `FileTests.java:147-153`; `run_out_WIcontains`, which `library_tests/Boolean.test:14` writes, is now implemented too (`FileTests.java:155-163`), but this batch writes `_contains`.

Forty-seven assertions. Every direction on every type; `widen` of a negative `ZZ32`, of the `ZZ32` minimum and of an `NN32` above 2^31; `narrow` in range on both sides, including at the exact boundaries 2^31-1, -2^31 and 2^32-1; `narrow` out of range on both sides in the `shouldOverflow` shape of `library_tests/Integer3.fss:17-24`, at 2^32, the `ZZ64` maximum and the `ZZ64` minimum on the signed side and at 2^63 and 2^64-1 on the unsigned side; `unsigned`/`signed` round trips at -1 and at the minimum of both `ZZ32` and `ZZ64`; `narrow` undoing `widen` on both `ZZ32` and `NN32`; and the two identities of `NumberPrintTest.fss:54-55`, `widen(unsigned(43))` and `unsigned(widen(43))`, asserted equal to each other as well as to 43, with the pair asserted again at -1 where they part company (4294967295 against 18446744073709551615).

Every operand is a typed binding and never a numeral inside the expression, which is `Integer3.fss:36-50`'s shape and the reason rung N gave for it: `INTEGERLITERALFOLDING` runs before `TYPECHECK` (`compiler/phases/PhaseOrder.java:57`), so an operand written as a numeral can be answered by the folder rather than by the prelude. `zMin` and `lMin` are written `-zMax - 1` over a hexadecimal maximum, as `IntegralOpsRungN.fss:88-89` and `:224-225` write them.

**Every `NN32`- and `NN64`-valued result is rendered through `.asZZ.asString`, not `.asString`.** Ledger row 326 is open on exactly this: `FNN32.toString` and `FNN64.toString` render a signed value, so `.asString` on an unsigned value above the signed half gives a negative string on the compiled path. #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Turn the raw compile/run outputs of run-ladder.sh into the ladder table.

Reads  explorations/compile-ladder/results.tsv  and  raw/<corpus>/<file>.{compile,run}
Writes explorations/compile-ladder/ladder.tsv    (one row per file, diffable)
       explorations/compile-ladder/summary.txt   (the counts and the rankings)

Phase vocabulary, and where each decision comes from:
  parse        a parse-stage refusal (Rats! "Syntax Error", the precedence
               resolver's "Resolution of operator ... failed")
  disambiguate an unresolved or ambiguous name (TypeDisambiguator.java:363,380
               "X is undefined."; "Type name may refer to";
               GraphRepository.java:417 "Could not find an implementation for API")
  typecheck    the Scala checker (TypeWellFormedChecker.scala:95,119
               "Unbound type:"; "Could not check call to"; "Ill-formed type")
  codegen      CodeGen.sayWhat (CodeGen.java:1550-1562 "Can't compile") or any
               CompilerError raised from the codegen packages
  link         `fortress run` fails to load or link the compiled component
  run          `fortress run` throws or exits non-zero
  pass         exit 0, no `fail`/`FAIL` in the output, no exception
               (the interpreter suite's own criterion, FileTests.java:367-371)
"""

import os, re, sys, collections

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
RAW = os.path.join(ROOT, "raw")

LOC = re.compile(r"^.*\.fs[si]:\d+:.*:$")

def first_error(text):
    """The first error message line, verbatim (without its location header)."""
    lines = text.splitlines()
    for i, ln in enumerate(lines):
        if LOC.match(ln.strip()) and i + 1 < len(lines):
            return lines[i + 1].strip()
    for ln in lines:
        s = ln.strip()
        if s.startswith("Exception in thread"):
            return s
    for ln in lines:
        s = ln.strip()
        if ("Error" in s or "Exception" in s or s.startswith("error")) and not s.startswith("at "):
            return s
    for ln in lines:
        s = ln.strip()
        if s:
            return s
    return ""

# A compile-time crash names its phase in the stack: compiler/phases/*Phase.execute.
PHASE_FRAME = re.compile(r"com\.sun\.fortress\.compiler\.phases\.(\w+)Phase\.execute")
PHASE_OF_FRAME = {
    "Grammar": "parse", "PreDisambiguationDesugar": "disambiguate",
    "Disambiguate": "disambiguate", "IntegerLiteralFolding": "disambiguate",
    "PreTypeCheckDesugar": "typecheck", "TypeCheck": "typecheck",
    "Desugar": "typecheck", "OverloadRewriting": "codegen",
    "CodeGeneration": "codegen", "EnvGeneration": "codegen", "Empty": "parse",
}

Five defects were measured in the course of this rung. One is repaired here and gated; three get provisional ledger rows because the specification is silent or because the repair is in Java outside a library rung; one is an open row already.

**D1, repaired here, home 1 — `NN64.coerce(x: NN32)` sign-extended.** Measured before the edit, `probes/probe-coerce-nn-preedit.txt`: an `NN32` holding 4294967295 coerced to `NN64` became 18446744073709551615, and one holding 2147483648 became 18446744071562067968. The specification settles it: `Specification/basic/conversions-coercions.tex:59-61` says coercion lets one "use a value of one type `T` as if it were a value of another type `U`", and `:73-83` that "given any value of type `T`, an appropriate value of type `U` can be computed to substitute for it" — a substitute that is a different number is not an appropriate one. Repaired by replacing `jIntToLong` with the zero-extending `jUnsignedIntToLong`, and gated by three assertions in `IntConversionsRungW.fss` (the `takesNN64` calls at 4294967295, 2147483648 and 43), each carrying `conversions-coercions.tex:73-75` in its message. The assertions are in place and pass.

**D2, deferred, home 3 — `narrow` out of range diverges between the two paths, and the specification is silent.** Measured both ways, `probes/probe-NarrowUnsigned.txt`: under `walk`, `narrow` of an `NN64` holding 2^64-1 gives 4294967295; on the compiled path it raises `fortress.CompilerBuiltin$IntegerOverflow` from `simpleUnsignedIntArith.toUnsignedIntOverflow(simpleUnsignedIntArith.java:27)` through `NN64.narrow` at `CompilerBuiltin.fss:874`. This is the divergence this rung's decision creates, deliberately and with its reasons above. No prose chapter names `narrow`, so nothing settles it; the home is a committed probe and provisional ledger row **W-2**, which says in as many words that it is here because the specification is silent.

**D3, deferred, home 3 — under `walk`, a signed `narrow` that overflows cannot be caught.** Measured both ways, `probes/probe-NarrowSigned.txt` and `probes/walk-narrow.txt`: the interpreter's `Int.rc` raises `error("Overflow of ZZ32 " + i)` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/glue/prim/Int.java:239-245`), which arrives as a `com.sun.fortress.exceptions.ProgramError` and is **not** caught by `try … catch e IntegerOverflow ⇒ …`, so a program that guards the conversion dies anyway; on the compiled path the same guard prints `true`. Here the specification does settle it, and against the interpreter: `Specification/basic/operators/opr-overview.tex:155` says an integer overflow throws an `IntegerOverflow`, and `basic/exceptions.tex:67-80` makes `IntegerOverflow` an ordinary `UncheckedException` in the hierarchy a `catch` clause matches. The repair is `Int.rc` raising a Fortress exception instead of calling `error`, which is Java and outside a library rung — rule 4's fourth case, so the rung lands and opens provisional ledger row **W-3**.

That defect cannot take home 2, and the reason is worth recording because it bounds where expected-failure tests can live. `shouldFail` is set from the file name only in the `.test`-driven suites — `FileTests.java:932`, `boolean shouldFail = s.startsWith("XXX")` inside `suiteFromListOfFiles` — and the interpreter corpus has no `.test` files at all (383 `.fss` and none), so `interpreterSuite` sets `shouldFail` from its own suite-level `expect_failure` argument instead (`FileTests.java:768` passes `false` for `tests`, and `:825-829` hands it to each `InterpreterTest`). An `XXX` name in `ProjectFortress/tests/` is honoured only in the exception path at `:346`, which tolerates a failure; nothing there turns red when such a file starts passing. So an interpreter-only defect has no gated expected-failure home in this tree, and a ledger row is the instrument rule 4 names for it.

**D4, deferred, home 3 — the interpreter's api declares `NN64.signed` returning `NN64`, and its own glue returns a `ZZ64`.** `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:461` declares `signed(self):NN64`; the body at `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:821-822` binds `UnsignedLong$ToLong`, which extends `U2L`, whose `applyMethod` returns `FLong.make(…)` — a `ZZ64` (`UnsignedLong.java:59-60`, `:224-228`). Measured, `probes/probe-SignedType.txt`: under `walk` as well as compiled, `signed` of an `NN64` holding 2^64-1 compares below a `ZZ64` zero, which only a signed value does; `ProjectFortress/tests/UnsignedTest.fss:219` asserts exactly that and passes. The interpreter never checks a declared return type, so the mis-declaration is invisible there. The specification does not name `signed`, so this is home 3: the probe is committed and provisional ledger row **W-1** carries it. This rung declares the compiler prelude's `NN64.signed` as `: ZZ64`, which is the corrected spelling and the deviation recorded in the provenance block.

**D5, already an open row — `NN32` and `NN64` render signed on the compiled path.** This is ledger row 326 and no new row is opened for it. Measured again here, `probes/probe-nn-render.txt`, with one fact the row does not yet carry: the *prelude getter* is bypassed too, not only Java's `toString`. `CompilerBuiltin.fss:749` defines `NN32.getter asString(): String = jUnsignedIntToString(jMakeZZ32FromNN32(self))` and `simpleUnsignedIntArith.unsignedIntToString` masks to 32 bits before calling `Long.toString` (`simpleUnsignedIntArith.java:19-23`, `:31-33`), so the getter, if it ran, would render 4294967295; the compiled run gives `-1`. In the same run `nAll > n43` is `true` and `nAll.asZZ.asString` is `4294967295`, so the value and the unsigned comparison are right and only the rendering is wrong, which is what row 326 says. It is not given home 2: `asString` appears nowhere in the specification (a grep of `Specification/` finds no occurrence), the nearest clause is `basic-lib/objects.tex:120-122` on `toString` returning a string that "textually represents" the object, and that is too weak a sentence to gate an assertion on. The row's note is amended instead.

## The ladder subset

`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-int-conversions/run-subset.sh` with `subset.txt`, a copy of `repair-r1-atomic-static/run-subset.sh` with the output directory and the ladder root moved inside this worktree (`LADDER_ROOT=$FORTRESS_HOME/tmp/ladder-W-{before,after}`, `SUB=…/rung-int-conversions/{before,after}`), so nothing shared is touched. Five files: the four the batch record names, plus `tests/testRR32.fss`, which is in the subset because its recorded first error in `explorations/compile-ladder/baseline-2026-09-19/raw/tests/testRR32.fss.compile` is `Variable narrow is not defined` — the instruction to sweep the baseline for files whose first error names one of this rung's names found it, and the record did not.

The before run was made with the two prelude files restored from `8590d7a9e`, in its own ladder root, and reproduces the baseline's five rows exactly. Raw outputs: `before/raw-ladder/tests/`, `after/raw-ladder/tests/`, with `before/results.tsv` and `after/results.tsv`.

| file | before | after | first error before | first error after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tests/fib13.fss` | disambiguate, 4 errors | **typecheck**, 12 errors | `Variable unsigned is not defined.` | `Could not check call to operator SQRT` |
| `tests/longPrim.fss` | disambiguate, 44 errors | disambiguate, 2 errors | `Variable widen is not defined.` | `Operator ? is not defined.` |
| `tests/UnsignedTest.fss` | disambiguate, 110 errors | disambiguate, 4 errors | `Variable unsigned is not defined.` | `Variable partitionL is not defined.` |
| `tests/NumberPrintTest.fss` | disambiguate, 10 errors | disambiguate, 1 error | `Variable big is not defined.` | `Variable big is not defined.` |
| `tests/testRR32.fss` | disambiguate, 26 errors | disambiguate, 10 errors | `Variable narrow is not defined.` | `Operator PLUS_UP is not defined.` |

The phases are `explorations/compile-ladder/classify.py`'s: `Variable X is not defined.` and `Operator X is not defined.` are disambiguate (`classify.py:82-86`), `Could not check call to …` is typecheck (`:87-95`). One file moves a phase, `fib13`, which is what the batch record predicted and the whole of it; nothing moved down, and every other file drops errors and stops on a name this rung is told by name to leave alone — `partitionL`, `big`, the `?` operator, the rounding operators.

`fib13` is worth one more line, because it shows the four names doing their work rather than merely existing. None of its twelve remaining errors mentions `widen`, `narrow`, `unsigned` or `signed`; four of them read "is not applicable to an argument of type `(NN32, IntLiteral, String)`" and four more "`(NN64, IntLiteral, String)`", so `unsigned(20)` resolved, coerced its `IntLiteral` argument without ambiguity, and delivered an `NN32` and an `NN64` to `fib13[\NN32\]` and `fib13[\NN64\]` as the program asks. What stops the file now is that `assert` has no overload taking those types and that `SQRT` and `/` are not applicable to an `IntLiteral` — pre-existing gaps in other areas.

## The greps step 6 asks for

Both corpora, for a competing declaration of each of the four names: `grep -rn '^\s*\(widen\|narrow\|unsigned\|signed\)\s*(self' ProjectFortress/tests/ ProjectFortress/*_tests/ Library/ ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/` gives the interpreter prelude's own declarations (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:695`, `:699`, `:765`, `:767`, `:819`, `:821`, `.fsi:434`, `:460-461`, `:493`, `:495`, `:532`, `:539-540`, `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss:442`, `:446`, `.fsi:105`, `:107`) and `RR64.narrow` (`FortressLibrary.fss:471`, `.fsi:365`, `FortressBuiltin.fss:77`), and from the test corpora exactly one file: `ProjectFortress/not_working_static_tests/BuiltinTest.fss:68,72`, which declares `widen` and `unsigned` inside a trait of its own in a corpus no gate target sweeps. No `library_tests/` or `compiler_tests/` file declares any of the four, so there is no repeat of the `MaybeTest9.fss` collision rung 1 lost a cycle to.

`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/` whole, not `compiler/` and `runtimeSystem/` alone: no hit for any of the four as a Fortress identifier. Every `widen` hit is the reserved word `widens` (`parser/Keyword.rats`, `parser/Method.rats`, `parser/MayNewlineHeader.rats`, `nodes/WhereCoerces.java`, `nodes/_SyntaxTransformationWhereCoerces.java`, `nodes_util/NodeFactory.java`, `scala_src/overloading/OverloadingOracle.scala`, `scala_src/typechecker/impls/Operators.scala`, `tools/FortressAstToConcrete.java`) and every `narrow` hit is `narrowToRange` or an unrelated word; `"widen"`, `"narrow"`, `"unsigned"` and `"signed"` as string literals appear nowhere. Nothing in `syntax_abstractions/` names them, which is the check rung M's find added to this step.

## Decisions, each with the alternative rejected

1. **`narrow` throws `IntegerOverflow` out of range on both sides.** Rejected: truncating on the unsigned side to match the interpreter and `UnsignedTest.fss:210-211`. Argued in full above; the cost of the choice is ledger row W-2 and the cost of the alternative would have been breaking a convention the file being edited follows at thirty-two sites.
2. **`NN64.signed` is declared `: ZZ64`.** Rejected: copying the interpreter api's `: NN64` (`FortressLibrary.fsi:461`). That spelling makes the function an identity on `NN64`, which is not what its own glue computes (`UnsignedLong.java:59-60`) and not what the interpreter's own test relies on (`UnsignedTest.fss:219`); and the compiler path has a type checker that would hold the declaration to its word. Recorded as a deviation and as ledger row W-1.
3. **One native binding is added, `simpleUnsignedIntArith.toLong`.** Rejected: writing the zero-extension in Fortress as a `BITAND` against a 4294967295 mask. The mask would have to arrive as a numeral, and numerals of exactly 32 bits are the subject of rows 317 and 325; paying that risk to avoid one line in an import block of forty-two bindings from the same class is a bad trade. The method is already public and is what every unsigned `ZZ32` operation in that class uses internally (`simpleUnsignedIntArith.java:19-23`).
4. **`NN64.coerce(x: NN32)` is repaired in this rung rather than deferred.** Rejected: leaving it and opening a row. It is a one-token change in a trait body this rung already owns, no other rung of the batch touches the file, and leaving it would have put two spellings of the same conversion in one trait giving different answers — `widen(x)` zero-extending and `coerce` sign-extending — which is the state the rung exists to end.
5. **The eight declarations go at the end of each trait body.** Rejected: putting them beside the `bitsAs*` getters they share a mechanism with. The interpreter's own api puts all six of its equivalents at the end of their traits (`FortressLibrary.fsi:493-495`, `:532`, `FortressBuiltin.fsi:105-107`), and following that keeps the diff a pure append inside each trait.
6. **The gated test renders `NN32` and `NN64` results through `.asZZ.asString`.** Rejected: `.asString`, which would have made the test assert ledger row 326's defect and fail for a reason that is not this rung's; and rejected: comparing values with `=` against constants built from the same four names, which would be circular. `asZZ` grounds each value in `ZZ`, whose rendering is measured correct in the same probe.

## What this rung did not do

`partitionL` (`FortressLibrary.fsi:491`), `partition` (`:1382`), `big`, `RR64.narrow(): RR32` (`.fsi:362`) and everything in `trait RR64`, `trait IntLiteral` and the tower are out of scope by name, and none was added even though `UnsignedTest`, `NumberPrintTest` and `testRR32` want them. Ledger row 326's repair is Java (`compiler/runtimeValues/FNN32.java:19-20`, `FNN64.java:20`) and stays open. Row 333 is another batch's Java slot. The interpreter-side repairs of W-1 and W-3 are Java in `interpreter/glue/prim/` and `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi`, and both are named in their rows with the fix.

`ant testFast` and `ant testSystem` were not run: the batch is gated once after the merge. One thing a reader of the gate should know in advance: this rung changes the *behaviour* of `NN64.coerce(x: NN32)`, not only adds declarations, so a gated test that relied on the sign-extended answer would move. A grep of `ProjectFortress/library_tests/` and `compiler_tests/` finds no file that coerces an `NN32` to `NN64` at all, and `library_tests/Integer.test`'s nine components are `ZZ32` and `ZZ64` only.

## One operational error, recorded

While restarting an aborted subset run at 05:48 I used `pkill -9 -f 'com.sun.fortress'`, a pattern that does not name a worktree, and there was a `fortress compile` of the parallel rung X running at the time in `/home/user/fortress-export`; it may have been killed. That agent had a compile running again two minutes later. Every later process action in this rung was restricted to a pattern containing this worktree's path. The lesson belongs in the batch prefix: a kill pattern in a shared container must name the worktree.

The before run was made with the two prelude files restored from `8590d7a9e`, in its own ladder root, and reproduces the baseline's five rows exactly. Raw outputs: `before/raw-ladder/tests/`, `after/raw-ladder/tests/`, with `before/results.tsv` and `after/results.tsv`.

| file | before | after | first error before | first error after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tests/fib13.fss` | disambiguate, 4 errors | **typecheck**, 12 errors | `Variable unsigned is not defined.` | `Could not check call to operator SQRT` |
| `tests/longPrim.fss` | disambiguate, 44 errors | disambiguate, 2 errors | `Variable widen is not defined.` | `Operator ? is not defined.` |
| `tests/UnsignedTest.fss` | disambiguate, 110 errors | disambiguate, 4 errors | `Variable unsigned is not defined.` | `Variable partitionL is not defined.` |
| `tests/NumberPrintTest.fss` | disambiguate, 10 errors | disambiguate, 1 error | `Variable big is not defined.` | `Variable big is not defined.` |
| `tests/testRR32.fss` | disambiguate, 26 errors | disambiguate, 10 errors | `Variable narrow is not defined.` | `Operator PLUS_UP is not defined.` |

The phases are `explorations/compile-ladder/classify.py`'s: `Variable X is not defined.` and `Operator X is not defined.` are disambiguate (`classify.py:82-86`), `Could not check call to …` is typecheck (`:87-95`). One file moves a phase, `fib13`, which is what the batch record predicted and the whole of it; nothing moved down, and every other file drops errors and stops on a name this rung is told by name to leave alone — `partitionL`, `big`, the `?` operator, the rounding operators.

`fib13` is worth one more line, because it shows the four names doing their work rather than merely existing. None of its twelve remaining errors mentions `widen`, `narrow`, `unsigned` or `signed`; four of them read "is not applicable to an argument of type `(NN32, IntLiteral, String)`" and four more "`(NN64, IntLiteral, String)`", so `unsigned(20)` resolved, coerced its `IntLiteral` argument without ambiguity, and delivered an `NN32` and an `NN64` to `fib13[\NN32\]` and `fib13[\NN64\]` as the program asks. What stops the file now is that `assert` has no overload taking those types and that `SQRT` and `/` are not applicable to an `IntLiteral` — pre-existing gaps in other areas.

## The greps step 6 asks for

Both corpora, for a competing declaration of each of the four names: `grep -rn '^\s*\(widen\|narrow\|unsigned\|signed\)\s*(self' ProjectFortress/tests/ ProjectFortress/*_tests/ Library/ ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/` gives the interpreter prelude's own declarations (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:695`, `:699`, `:765`, `:767`, `:819`, `:821`, `.fsi:434`, `:460-461`, `:493`, `:495`, `:532`, `:539-540`, `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss:442`, `:446`, `.fsi:105`, `:107`) and `RR64.narrow` (`FortressLibrary.fss:471`, `.fsi:365`, `FortressBuiltin.fss:77`), and from the test corpora exactly one file: `ProjectFortress/not_working_static_tests/BuiltinTest.fss:68,72`, which declares `widen` and `unsigned` inside a trait of its own in a corpus no gate target sweeps. No `library_tests/` or `compiler_tests/` file declares any of the four, so there is no repeat of the `MaybeTest9.fss` collision rung 1 lost a cycle to.

`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/` whole, not `compiler/` and `runtimeSystem/` alone: no hit for any of the four as a Fortress identifier. Every `widen` hit is the reserved word `widens` (`parser/Keyword.rats`, `parser/Method.rats`, `parser/MayNewlineHeader.rats`, `nodes/WhereCoerces.java`, `nodes/_SyntaxTransformationWhereCoerces.java`, `nodes_util/NodeFactory.java`, `scala_src/overloading/OverloadingOracle.scala`, `scala_src/typechecker/impls/Operators.scala`, `tools/FortressAstToConcrete.java`) and every `narrow` hit is `narrowToRange` or an unrelated word; `"widen"`, `"narrow"`, `"unsigned"` and `"signed"` as string literals appear nowhere. Nothing in `syntax_abstractions/` names them, which is the check rung M's find added to this step.

## Decisions, each with the alternative rejected

1. **`narrow` throws `IntegerOverflow` out of range on both sides.** Rejected: truncating on the unsigned side to match the interpreter and `UnsignedTest.fss:210-211`. Argued in full above; the cost of the choice is ledger row W-2 and the cost of the alternative would have been breaking a convention the file being edited follows at thirty-two sites.
2. **`NN64.signed` is declared `: ZZ64`.** Rejected: copying the interpreter api's `: NN64` (`FortressLibrary.fsi:461`). That spelling makes the function an identity on `NN64`, which is not what its own glue computes (`UnsignedLong.java:59-60`) and not what the interpreter's own test relies on (`UnsignedTest.fss:219`); and the compiler path has a type checker that would hold the declaration to its word. Recorded as a deviation and as ledger row W-1.
3. **One native binding is added, `simpleUnsignedIntArith.toLong`.** Rejected: writing the zero-extension in Fortress as a `BITAND` against a 4294967295 mask. The mask would have to arrive as a numeral, and numerals of exactly 32 bits are the subject of rows 317 and 325; paying that risk to avoid one line in an import block of forty-two bindings from the same class is a bad trade. The method is already public and is what every unsigned `ZZ32` operation in that class uses internally (`simpleUnsignedIntArith.java:19-23`).
4. **`NN64.coerce(x: NN32)` is repaired in this rung rather than deferred.** Rejected: leaving it and opening a row. It is a one-token change in a trait body this rung already owns, no other rung of the batch touches the file, and leaving it would have put two spellings of the same conversion in one trait giving different answers — `widen(x)` zero-extending and `coerce` sign-extending — which is the state the rung exists to end.
5. **The eight declarations go at the end of each trait body.** Rejected: putting them beside the `bitsAs*` getters they share a mechanism with. The interpreter's own api puts all six of its equivalents at the end of their traits (`FortressLibrary.fsi:493-495`, `:532`, `FortressBuiltin.fsi:105-107`), and following that keeps the diff a pure append inside each trait.
6. **The gated test renders `NN32` and `NN64` results through `.asZZ.asString`.** Rejected: `.asString`, which would have made the test assert ledger row 326's defect and fail for a reason that is not this rung's; and rejected: comparing values with `=` against constants built from the same four names, which would be circular. `asZZ` grounds each value in `ZZ`, whose rendering is measured correct in the same probe.

## What this rung did not do

`partitionL` (`FortressLibrary.fsi:491`), `partition` (`:1382`), `big`, `RR64.narrow(): RR32` (`.fsi:362`) and everything in `trait RR64`, `trait IntLiteral` and the tower are out of scope by name, and none was added even though `UnsignedTest`, `NumberPrintTest` and `testRR32` want them. Ledger row 326's repair is Java (`compiler/runtimeValues/FNN32.java:19-20`, `FNN64.java:20`) and stays open. Row 333 is another batch's Java slot. The interpreter-side repairs of W-1 and W-3 are Java in `interpreter/glue/prim/` and `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi`, and both are named in their rows with the fix.

`ant testFast` and `ant testSystem` were not run: the batch is gated once after the merge. One thing a reader of the gate should know in advance: this rung changes the *behaviour* of `NN64.coerce(x: NN32)`, not only adds declarations, so a gated test that relied on the sign-extended answer would move. A grep of `ProjectFortress/library_tests/` and `compiler_tests/` finds no file that coerces an `NN32` to `NN64` at all, and `library_tests/Integer.test`'s nine components are `ZZ32` and `ZZ64` only.

## One operational error, recorded

While restarting an aborted subset run at 05:48 I used `pkill -9 -f 'com.sun.fortress'`, a pattern that does not name a worktree, and there was a `fortress compile` of the parallel rung X running at the time in `/home/user/fortress-export`; it may have been killed. That agent had a compile running again two minutes later. Every later process action in this rung was restricted to a pattern containing this worktree's path. The lesson belongs in the batch prefix: a kill pattern in a shared container must name the worktree.
